# R285 — final functional coverage check against official v0.1.43

Date: 2026-10-12 (JST). Read-only comparison of the supplied stable adoption snapshot `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/sync-upstream-v0143-server-lifecycle-20261012` at `501dd9ef8fa5a9d8a357181bc0de3c3229f65aa3` with official pristine v0.1.43 at `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`. Parent reports the xe0.1.42 HEAD remains `da3d426079019daa6e01388d03b0d94ae67070b7`. Registry v166 records 792 completed research reports. I read R277, R253, R331, the closed v0.1.43 server-completion report and its result index, then compared relevant source and file presence. No source edits, test/build execution, GPU/model work, process checks, cleanup, service operation, Git mutation, or access to the in-flight WCO occurred.

## Finding

The selected single-device XeStrata server/API/setup import is substantially complete, and the latest stable source includes the final lifecycle/frontend ports from commit `fcb86a77`. The closed server-completion report records 555 fake-engine/HTTP tests (544 passed, 11 skipped), new lifecycle/parser/content/tool-order tests passing, and no GPU/model inference. That is host regression evidence, not Windows process-lifecycle or hardware qualification.

This final pass did identify two remaining user-visible cross-platform/frontend coverage gaps against the official source: Windows child-process containment/no-throttling, and the Monitor's conversation-cache detail card. Neither is a CUDA/HIP inference issue. The first affects Windows server lifecycle; the second affects visibility of a cache feature implemented by the selected engine. I found no new missing required OpenAI/Anthropic endpoint or setup flow. The unresolved setup evidence limits from R253 remain as limits, not new source changes.

## Function-to-source coverage

| Function area | Current adoption evidence | Result and boundary |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages, and OpenAI Responses | `serve/server.py` routes the three APIs; `serve/frontend.py`, `serve/responses.py`, and `serve/logit_bias.py` carry the shared request/response behavior. `serve/test_context_overflow.py`, `serve/test_logit_bias.py`, server tests, and the closed result set cover mock/fake-engine protocol paths. | Present. Unsupported nonempty `logit_bias` fails closed unless the engine advertises support; the SYCL engine does not claim CUDA/HIP sampler behavior. |
| Context and reasoning configuration | `serve/server.py` imports config `reasoning_effort`, supports launcher-aware `effort_position=end`, and classifies context overflow; `serve/test_config_effort.py` and `serve/test_context_overflow.py` are present. | Present at source and host-test level. Does not establish a live model response. |
| SAVE admission retry / memory and session behavior | `serve/session_save_retry.py` and its HTTP/fake-engine tests are present. Native memory guard and SAVE reclaim integration are included in the 0691 import. Conversation-file implementation is retained rather than replaced. | Present as selected shared behavior; SAVE/RESTORE device/runtime completion is not inferred from Python tests. |
| Queue and startup lifecycle | The `fcb86a77` delta adds bounded SSE keepalives for a queued single-turn request and fixes lazy/restart READY timeout handling, including the uninitialized slot condition case. Dedicated `serve/test_queue_keepalive.py` and `serve/test_ready_timeout.py` were added. | Present. The closed completion report records these tests passing. Windows process-tree containment remains separately absent (below). |
| Content parts, tool order, and streaming parser | `fcb86a77` adds ignored-unknown-content debug handling while retaining readable content/refusal, bounded tool-order memory, whitespace-tolerant tool names, quoted `</think>` handling, and block-based long-line accumulation. Focused frontend/parser/tool tests are present. | Present for these source behaviors; no new endpoint gap found. |
| Setup archive recovery and attach-only HTTP benchmark offer | `setup.py` includes damaged-ZIP and `.done` cleanup/retry and an opt-in display-only HTTP benchmark command; `tools/test_setup_llama_archive.py` and `tools/test_setup_http_bench_offer.py` exist. | Present. R253's prior evidence gaps remain: Windows `cmd.exe` rendering for the optional benchmark command was not established, and archive tests do not establish validation of a wrong/multiple-root or missing-member but valid-CRC archive before replacing the old tree. These are not evidence that the pinned archive is bad. |
| Web model switching and ordinary Monitor | Current `serve/web/app.js`, `index.html`, and `server.py` include XeStrata's custom `model_switcher` UI/endpoint and current engine/system metrics. | Custom behavior present. The official Monitor's separate conversation-cache card is absent (details below). |
| Multi-GPU replicas and Linux replica CPU partitioning | Official `serve/replicas.py`, `serve/cpu_affinity.py`, and replica startup path are absent from the adoption snapshot. | Deliberately outside the one-device acceptance target; this is opt-in data-parallel service functionality and should not be implied as supported. |
| Windows prevent-sleep opt-in | Official `serve/keepawake.py` and its server hookup are absent. | Optional platform setting (`prevent_sleep`), not a default single-device serving prerequisite. |
| Backend-specific kernel, profile, and tuning changes | The top-level XeStrata acceptance build compiles its own `src/program/generate.cpp` and `src/kernels/xe/*`; it does not compile the official legacy `sycl/` subtree. | CUDA/HIP inference work is excluded as instructed. The official `sycl/setup_intel.py`/`data/expert-profile-sycl.bin` work is not a missing function in this compiled acceptance path; the XeStrata path uses its own profile/build flow. No performance parity claim follows. |

## Remaining gaps

### Windows process containment

Official v0.1.43 contains `serve/winjob.py` (`8fff65cf850e108b84ab06c3fb44a68b947b0f4834ce5880139ada5dfb11a749`). It creates a Windows Job Object configured to terminate contained child processes when the server's last job handle closes, and opts the server and children out of Windows power throttling. Official `serve/server.py` imports `contain` and calls it after engine and vision-encoder process creation; official `serve/mcp.py` also calls it for MCP children. The current adoption source has no `serve/winjob.py`, no `contain` imports/calls in those paths, and no `serve/test_winjob.py`.

Current `serve/server.py` starts the engine and vision subprocesses through `popen` without the job-object attachment. Current `serve/mcp.py` uses `start_new_session=True` and a process-group cleanup path, but that does not provide the official Windows kill-on-job-close contract for abrupt server exit; its cleanup path is not a substitute for containment after a crash/console close. This is an actual Windows service-lifecycle difference in a repository that supports Windows, not evidence of a failure on this Linux Xe run. The release's own description is at `serve/winjob.py:1-8`; official attach call sites are `serve/server.py:63,673,2029` and `serve/mcp.py:34,110`. Current relevant process-start points are `serve/server.py:671` (engine), vision `_start`, and `serve/mcp.py:100-107`.

### Conversation-cache Monitor detail

Official `serve/server.py` builds `conversation_cache_view(...)` and includes it in the authorized JSON Monitor metrics (`server.py:561-571,3325`); official `serve/web/index.html:129-137` and `serve/web/app.js:194-220` render parked slots, byte budget, reuse totals and the last park/restore event. The current engine still has `--conversation-cache-mib`/slot controls and emits park/restore records (`src/program/generate.cpp:459-460,2363-2370,8535`), while current `serve/server.py` still parses per-request `reused` values and exposes totals. But current `serve/server.py` has no `conversation_cache_view`/`conversation_cache` Monitor field, and current `serve/web/index.html`/`app.js` have no `cc-card` or `renderConvCache`. The adopted app retains an overall reused-token summary, but removes the richer parked-cache state display and the per-request reused column. This leaves a real Monitor-information gap for users of the native conversation-cache feature, not an inference or storage capability gap. A future port would need to preserve the XeStrata model-switcher additions while adding the cache view; R285 made no edits.

## Exclusions and evidence limits

- `replicas.py`/`cpu_affinity.py` implement optional multi-GPU data-parallel replicas, not the requested one-GPU service. They remain outside this adoption target; their absence must not be read as feature parity for replica configurations.
- `keepawake.py` implements the explicit Windows `prevent_sleep` opt-in. It is not enabled by default. The Windows child containment feature above is different: official `contain()` is called by default for engine, vision, and MCP children.
- The full host result was read from the closed `bench/results/2026-10-12-v0143-server-completion/REPORT.md` and `results.json`; no tests were rerun. It reports 555 tests, 544 pass, 11 skip, `gpu_executed=false`, `model_executed=false`. The WN engine/build/setup/data source-equivalence receipt states 318 selected source files match 0691; this does not prove parity with the official CUDA/HIP or legacy SYCL implementations.
- Setup archive and Windows display-command concerns were already recorded in R253 as test/compatibility scope gaps. This report does not re-open those as newly discovered features or assert an observed setup failure.
- No Windows execution was performed; the Windows Job Object difference is source-derived. No model/GPU/API performance behavior is claimed.

Current source SHA-256: `serve/server.py` `19a340bb2f277a0ebd57fd62ebcb76a68943d30623054186b89146885f8784bc`; `serve/mcp.py` `f3d9f5dafa1d9c1fb71a6bb2b09d9288fde20fe04f1f88c027dc45f3d283c2b7`; `serve/frontend.py` `fe95b91292ab0060e77bcdc88a72ed905a7190fd7cb6b229499486269248aa0a`; `serve/web/app.js` `50c575df627651b6c1a92a9d077d484d305f2e214a0032dc48c3390e79e65855`; `serve/web/index.html` `b5b4d322109500dae5f547b93fe30df7cad060af2fa8103695d5ef5a96212493`; `setup.py` `c537e11811da54bea26e8feda28c9252054e13465ce4e68f16ffcfdffe22f462`; `serve/runconfig.py` `f303263f51e54795e8dae3d75082322216d49993bd5536a0027a455e4fa82969`.
